Cycling Power Estimator

Estimate cycling power in watts from speed, rider weight, and gradient using the standard physics model.

Model: ½ρCdA·v³ (aero, CdA 0.32) + Crr·m·g·v (rolling, Crr 0.005) + m·g·grade·v (gravity).

General information only — not medical advice. Consult a professional for personal guidance.

📖 How to use

  1. Enter your average speed in km/h.
  2. Enter rider weight and bike weight in kg.
  3. Enter the average gradient in percent (negative for descents).
  4. Press Calculate to see estimated watts and the breakdown.

❓ Frequently asked questions

How is power estimated?

Power overcomes three resistances: aerodynamic drag, rolling resistance, and gravity on hills. The model sums all three.

What is a good wattage?

Flat-road cruising is usually 100–200 W, a strong club rider holds 250–300 W, and pros exceed 400 W on climbs.

Is this as accurate as a power meter?

An estimate only — it cannot replace a power meter. Wind, position, and tires change real values by 10–20%.
